claims.claim: Gilgamesh is 'two-thirds divine and one-third human', the son of the goddess Ninsun and the king Lugalbanda.
claims.evidence: Gilgamesh Tablet I (Thompson 1928, read in full); Death of Gilgamesh (ETCSL t.1.8.1.3, read in full).

claims.claim: There is no marriage narrative for Gilgamesh's parents — the parentage is stated as a fact about the hero's nature, not as a story of a god taking a human wife.
claims.evidence: Same sources as clm-hc-001; the absence of a marriage narrative is a property of the verified texts.

claims.claim: Šulgi of Ur calls himself 'a child born of Ninsun', 'brother and friend' of Gilgamesh, and the spouse of Inanna; his historical parents were Ur-Nammu and a human queen.
claims.evidence: Šulgi A (ETCSL t.2.4.2.01, read in full); Šulgi C (ETCSL t.2.4.2.03, read in full).

claims.claim: Šulgi's divine parentage is royal ideology — a status claim made by a king about himself — not a narrative of a god marrying a woman.
claims.evidence: Same sources as clm-hc-004; the claim is the king's own propaganda in his own hymns.

claims.claim: The apkallu (seven sages) are advisers and teachers of kings, not husbands or fathers of a race.
claims.evidence: Gilgamesh I prologue; Šulgi C (seven wisdoms); Berossus's Oannes (teaches letters and arts) — all read in full.

claims.claim: Berossus's Babyloniaca (c. 290 BCE) records Oannes teaching letters and arts, ten kings reigning 432,000 years before the flood, a flood without a moral cause, and Xisuthrus saved for his piety.
claims.evidence: Berossus fragments (Wikisource, read in full as transmitted).

claims.claim: Eridu Genesis: the divine assembly decides the destruction of mankind — 'the verdict, the word of the divine assembly, cannot be revoked' — and no moral cause is stated in the preserved text.
claims.evidence: Eridu Genesis (ETCSL t.1.7.4, Segment C, read in full).

claims.claim: Gilgamesh XI: the flood is decided in 'the Assemblage of Gods'; the gods are terrified by the flood they unleashed; Ishtar laments; Ea rebukes Enlil for the unreasoned flood.
claims.evidence: Gilgamesh XI (Thompson 1928, read in full).

claims.claim: At Ugarit the gods are a family: Baal 'called the seventy sons of Asherah' (KTU 1.4 VI 46); 'sons of El' (bn ʾil) is the closest linguistic parallel to bənê hāʾĕlōhîm in the ANE.
claims.evidence: Baal Cycle KTU 1.3–1.4 (Good Works Library 2026 translation, cross-checked against Wyatt 2010 and the transliteration ṣḥ šbʿm bn ʾaṯrt). Caveat: Smith & Pitard 2009 / Wyatt 2002 not opened.

claims.claim: No ANE text describes a divine being marrying a human woman and producing offspring. The specific motif of Gen 6:2 has no ANE parallel.
claims.evidence: The absence is established by the survey in dossier §5.1 (Gilgamesh, Šulgi, apkallu, Berossus, Eridu Genesis, Gilgamesh XI, Ugarit) — every candidate was read and none contains the motif.

claims.claim: The divine council is genuine ANE background that supports 'sons of God' as a linguistic (divine-court) option; it does not settle the interpretation, and no Ugaritic god takes a human wife.
claims.evidence: Dossier §5.2 (Eridu Genesis, Gilgamesh XI, KTU 1.4). The limit — the assembly decides, it does not marry — is established by the same texts.

claims.claim: Gilgamesh Tablet XI has been verified in full from R. Campbell Thompson's 1928 translation, and 'the gods gathered like flies' is confirmed verbatim.
claims.evidence: Thompson 1928, read in full. Adapted from the dossier row: the cross-dossier flag (the Cain and Abel dossier §3.5c 'NOT-INDEPENDENTLY-VERIFIED' label for Gilgamesh XI is now stale) is not asserted in this claim; it stays in the dossier for the EM to action.

claims.claim: In Gilgamesh XI the flood is decided without a moral cause; the gods are frightened and hungry after it; Ea rebukes Enlil for excess ('on the sinner lay his sin, on the transgressor lay his transgression' — a rebuke about excess, not a moral cause for the flood).
claims.evidence: Gilgamesh XI (Thompson 1928, read in full).

claims.claim: In Eridu Genesis the flood is a divine decision stated without a moral indictment of humanity in the preserved text.
claims.evidence: Eridu Genesis (ETCSL t.1.7.4, read in full).

claims.claim: In Berossus the flood comes without a moral cause, and Xisuthrus is saved for his piety.
claims.evidence: Berossus fragments (Wikisource, read in full as transmitted).

claims.claim: The flood traditions bear on Gen 6:5–7 in exactly one way: as a contrast. In Mesopotamia the flood is a divine decision without a moral indictment; in Genesis it is the consequence of a stated moral cause, and God is grieved, not frightened or hungry.
claims.evidence: Dossier §5.3 (Gilgamesh XI, Eridu Genesis, Berossus — all read in full). Atrahasis is part of the dossier's contrast survey but is not cited here — no registry entry exists for it; the contrast rests on the three cited traditions. The contrast is this dossier's synthesis of verified material.

claims.claim: No ANE text describes a race of giants called Nephilim. The Nephilim are a biblical subject, not an ANE one.
claims.evidence: The absence is established by the survey in dossier §5.4 (Anakim, rpum, Humbaba, Berossus fragment, 1 Enoch, Book of Giants) — every candidate was checked and none is an ANE Nephilim race. The rpum, Humbaba, 1 Enoch, and Book of Giants candidates are recorded in the dossier only; none is cited as a source here.

claims.claim: The Anakim appear in no ANE text; Num 13:33 is the only biblical link between the Nephilim and the Anakim.
claims.evidence: The ANE absence is established by the survey; the biblical link is verified from the stored KJV (Num 13:33).

claims.claim: Enlil and Namzitarra sets the limit of human life at 120 years: '120 years are the years of mankind… from the day that mankind exists until today'. The same number (120), the sexagesimal system (2 × 60), and a wisdom context (a reflection on life's brevity), not a judgment.
claims.evidence: Verified through Sibbing-Plantholt 2021 (peer-reviewed article, read in full, quoting Klein 1990, Cohen 2013, Alster 2005). Caveat: the cuneiform text itself was not opened. The parallel is proposed, not established.

claims.claim: In Enlil and Namzitarra the 120-year limit is presented as fixed from mankind's beginning, not newly imposed for wrongdoing.
claims.evidence: As quoted in Sibbing-Plantholt 2021 (read in full).

claims.claim: BDB (H430 sense 1c) records all three readings of 'sons of God' and their holders in a single entry: angelic (LXX, Enoch & Jubilees, Philo, Jude 1:6, 2 Pet 2:4, Josephus, 'most ancient fathers and modern critics'); 'sons of princes, mighty men' (Onkelos and the Rabbis); 'sons of God, the pious' (Theodoret, Chrysostom, Jerome, Augustine, Luther, Calvin, Hengstenberg).
claims.evidence: BDB H430 (BibleHub, read in full). This is BDB's record, not this dossier's endorsement.

claims.claim: BDB (H1121 sense 1d) classifies bənê hāʾĕlōhîm as supernatural beings ('sons of God, angels'), citing Gen 6:2, 6:4; Job 1:6, 2:1, 38:7.
claims.evidence: BDB H1121 (BibleHub, read in full). This is BDB's classification, not this dossier's endorsement.

claims.claim: BDB (H1323 sense 1a) glosses bənôt hāʾādām as human women, citing Gen 6:2, 6:4.
claims.evidence: BDB H1323 (BibleHub, read in full).

claims.claim: BDB (H5303) renders nəpîlîm 'giants' (after LXX γίγαντες / Vulgate gigantes) and states the etymology is 'dubious'. 'Fallen ones' is NOT what BDB asserts — that is Strong's gloss, not BDB's.
claims.evidence: BDB H5303 (BibleHub, read in full).

claims.claim: The text does not say the Nephilim are the children of the unions; the relationship is unstated.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV 6:4. A textual silence, verified by reading the verse.

claims.claim: yādôn (H1777) ×1 in Gen 6:3; BDB: 'verb dubious', four readings listed; 'strive' (KJV) is 'hardly justified' by BDB's own account. Endpoint 24 (lemma dîn).
claims.evidence: OL word rows + BDB H1777 (BibleHub, read in full). This is BDB's judgment, not this dossier's endorsement of any of the four readings.

claims.claim: māḥâ (H4229) ×1 in Gen 6:7; BDB Qal sense 3 ('blot out = exterminate') cites Gen 6:7 with Gen 7:4.
claims.evidence: OL word rows + BDB H4229 (BibleHub, read in full).

claims.claim: No specific sins are named in 6:5 — no 'violence' (that is Gen 6:11–13, Flood event).
claims.evidence: Stored KJV 6:5. A textual silence, verified by reading the verse.

claims.claim: No reason is given for Noah finding favour in 6:8; the text does not say Noah was righteous here — that is Gen 6:9 (Ark event).
claims.evidence: Stored KJV 6:8. A textual silence, verified by reading the verse.

claims.claim: The angelic/heavenly reading is held by Ryle, Skinner, Justin Martyr, Tertullian, Irenaeus, Athenagoras, Eusebius (tentatively), Philo (literal reading), Josephus, and Pseudo-Jonathan; BDB's own classification (H1121 sense 1d) is the angelic reading.
claims.evidence: Ryle, Skinner (dossier §8.1); Justin, Tertullian, Irenaeus, Athenagoras, Eusebius (dossier §8.4 — Justin, Second Apology 5; Tertullian, Veiling 7; Irenaeus, Demonstration 18; Athenagoras, Plea 24–25; Eusebius, Preparation V.4, tentative); Philo, De Gigantibus; Josephus, Antiquities 1.3.1; Pseudo-Jonathan 6:2–4 (dossier §8.3) — all read in full; the fathers and Jewish sources other than the registered ones are named here with dossier §12.1 references, following the Seth precedent for evidence naming works outside the registry. The reading itself is debated; the holders are verified.

claims.claim: Westermann and Gunkel hold a refinement inside the heavenly family: the sons are divine beings of lower rank, expressly not angels; the 'angel' label entered through the LXX and 1 Enoch.
claims.evidence: Westermann pp. 363–375 (read in full); Gunkel pp. 55–63 (read in full). The prose omits the 1 Enoch channel per the conservative decision (1 Enoch material stays dossier-only); the register records the full position.

claims.claim: The Sethite reading is held by Keil & Delitzsch, JFB, Clarke, Julius Africanus (as his preferred reading), and Augustine (its fullest argued form); BDB records the 'pious' reading (Theodoret, Chrysostom, Jerome, Augustine, Luther, Calvin, Hengstenberg) but does NOT name 'Sethites'.
claims.evidence: Keil, JFB, Clarke (dossier §8.1); Africanus, Fragments 2 and 4; Augustine, City of God XV.22–25 (dossier §8.4) — all read in full. BDB H430 (read in full).

claims.claim: The royal/powerful-figures reading is held as a primary identification by the Targumic and rabbinic tradition (Onkelos, Rashi, Ramban, Genesis Rabbah 26:5; Neofiti main text, second-hand); in the Christian commentaries it appears only as a secondary nuance (JFB, citing Onkelos) or a reported alternative (Clarke, citing Dr. Wall); it is explicitly rejected by Keil, Ryle, and Gunkel.
claims.evidence: Onkelos, Rashi, Ramban, Genesis Rabbah 26:5 (dossier §8.3 — read in full); Neofiti second-hand via Newman 1984 citing Diez Macho (dossier §12.2, entry 1); JFB, Clarke, Keil, Ryle, Gunkel (dossier §8.1 — read in full). The Neofiti rendering is labelled second-hand here.

claims.claim: Matt 22:30 ('in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven') is cited as a counter-text against the angelic reading, by Keil and JFB.
claims.evidence: Keil and JFB (read in full). This is their argument, recorded as such.

claims.claim: The identical phrase bənê hāʾĕlōhîm in Job 1:6, 2:1, and 38:7 denotes heavenly beings presenting themselves before the LORD.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV (Job 1:6, 2:1, 38:7) + BDB H1121 sense 1d (read in full).

claims.claim: The Nephilim are 'fallen ones' / apostates (from nāpal): held by Clarke ('the fallen apostates'), JFB (in part, as an alternative), and Keil ('invaders' / 'tyrants', from nāpal in the sense of 'falling upon' others).
claims.evidence: Clarke, JFB, Keil (read in full). The reading is debated; the holders are verified.

claims.claim: The Nephilim are 'giants' (LXX γίγαντες): held by Ryle, Skinner, Gunkel, Onkelos (gibbaraya), and the Jewish Encyclopedia 'Giants' article.
claims.evidence: Ryle, Skinner, Gunkel, Onkelos (read in full); Jewish Encyclopedia 'Giants' (read in full, dossier §12.1 entry 22). The reading is debated; the holders are verified.

claims.claim: The etymology of nəpîlîm is lost / dubious: held by Ryle ('the etymology is lost'), BDB ('dubious'), and Skinner (the derivation is uncertain).
claims.evidence: Ryle, BDB H5303, Skinner (all read in full).

claims.claim: The Nephilim pre-exist the unions and are distinct from the gibbōrîm offspring: held by Keil, and by JFB in a weaker form.
claims.evidence: Keil, JFB (read in full). The reading is debated; the holders are verified.

claims.claim: The Nephilim are the offspring of the unions, identified with the gibbōrîm: held by Skinner and Gunkel.
claims.evidence: Skinner, Gunkel (read in full). The reading is debated; the holders are verified.

claims.claim: 'Also after that' (6:4) means before the Flood, in the generation of Enosh (Rashi; Genesis Rabbah 26:7) — vs. after the Flood, the sons of Anak (Ibn Ezra). The scope of ʾaḥărê-kēn is ambiguous and the text does not resolve it.
claims.evidence: Rashi, Genesis Rabbah 26:7, Ibn Ezra (all read in full). The disagreement is the finding; the text's ambiguity is verified by reading 6:4.

claims.claim: The 120 years are a countdown / respite before the Flood (a period of grace, a time allowed for repentance): held by Keil, JFB, Clarke, Augustine, and Africanus; and by Onkelos, Pseudo-Jonathan, Rashi, Ibn Ezra (endorsing Onkelos), and Ramban.
claims.evidence: Keil, JFB, Clarke (dossier §8.1); Augustine, Africanus (dossier §8.4); Onkelos, Pseudo-Jonathan, Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Ramban (dossier §8.3) — all read in full. The reading is debated; the holders are verified.

claims.claim: The 120 years are a lifespan cap / maximum (the new limit of human life): held by Skinner, Gunkel, and Westermann.
claims.evidence: Skinner, Gunkel (read in full); Westermann pp. 363–375 (read in full). The reading is debated; the holders are verified.

claims.claim: Ryle is genuinely undecided on the 120 years, finding both readings objectionable.
claims.evidence: Ryle (read in full).

claims.claim: Hendel's text-critical judgment on 6:3: MT yādôn is attested in M and S; yādûr ('abide/remain') is attested in 4QCommGenᵃ (4Q252), the LXX, Targum Onkelos, the Syriac, the Vulgate, and Jubilees 5:8; Hendel judges MT's reading a 'linguistic modernization, or perhaps graphic confusion' (nun/resh). Hendel does not discuss the Nephilim by name and takes no position on the three 'sons of God' interpretations.
claims.evidence: Hendel 1998, pp. 132–134 (archive.org community-texts PDF, read in full). Text-critical only. The prose names two of the six witnesses (Dead Sea Scrolls, Greek version); the full witness list is recorded here.

claims.claim: The Gen 5 lifespans exceed 120 for generations after Gen 6:3 (Methuselah 969, Jared 962, Noah 950) — a textual problem for the lifespan reading. Skinner handles it by assigning the Gen 5 figures to P and Gen 6:3 to J; Gunkel calls the respite reading an evasion. The problem is recorded, not resolved.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV (Gen 5) + Skinner, Gunkel (read in full).

claims.claim: Every commentator who treats 6:6–7 calls the language anthropomorphic / anthropopathic — a human way of speaking about God, not a change in God's nature.
claims.evidence: Keil, Ryle, Skinner, Gunkel, JFB, Clarke, Augustine (all read in full). The shared framing is the finding.

claims.claim: The emphases differ: Keil (the pain of divine love, citing Calvin); Ryle (two scriptural representations — 1 Sam 15:29 and 15:11 — both true); Skinner (unusually strong anthropopathy, felt inadequate yet retained); Gunkel ('had He known… He would certainly not have created them'); JFB (a change of visible procedure, not of purpose); Clarke (evidence the sins were voluntary); Augustine (unchangeable judgement in human language).
claims.evidence: Keil, Ryle, Skinner, Gunkel, JFB, Clarke, Augustine (all read in full). Each position is recorded as that author's.

claims.claim: 'But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD' (6:8) is the passage's hinge, and the verse gives no reason for Noah's favour.
claims.evidence: Stored KJV 6:8. A textual silence, verified by reading the verse.

connections.note: The primary account: men multiply and daughters are born; the sons of God take wives; the 120 years; the Nephilim and the mighty men of old; human wickedness; divine grief and the announced judgment; and Noah finding grace. The passage gives no date and names no place.

The genealogy is the event's immediate background: it closes with Noah's birth (5:28–29) and Noah's 500 years at his sons' birth (5:32). The Gen 5 lifespans bear on the 120-years question, exceeding 120 for generations.
The sequel: 'Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God' (6:9) is the Ark event's characterisation, not this event's. One-way link; the Ark event does not link back.

The identical phrase 'sons of God' denotes heavenly beings presenting themselves before the LORD: 'there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD' (1:6; repeated at 2:1). The strongest intra-biblical evidence for the angelic reading.
'When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?' The identical phrase, heavenly beings at creation.

The only other occurrence of Nephilim: 'And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants.' Cautions: the spies' report is their own, possibly exaggerated, account; 'come of' indicates descent as claimed, not identity; the Anakim as distinct from the Nephilim is not verified.

Reception: 'God standeth in the congregation of the mighty... I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.' The phrase is 'children of the most High' (bənê ʿelyôn), not 'sons of God' — a different phrase, and the referent is disputed.
Reception: 'the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation.' The angelic reading's New Testament anchor; probable because the verse does not cite Genesis 6.

Reception: 'God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell... and spared not the old world, but saved Noah.' Angels and the Flood in one breath; the angelic reading's New Testament anchor.

Reception: 'as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be... they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark.' Jesus's own reference to the days of Noah, including marrying and giving in marriage.

The Sethite reading's anchor: 'then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.' The Sethite line as the line that calls on the LORD; probable because the verse does not name Seth's line as 'sons of God'.

review.notes: Draft 2026-11-16 (branch content/biblical-history-humanitys-corruption, base main 289f264; PR #196 merged). Stage 1 dossier 2026-11-16 (three parallel researchers: ANE parallels + Nephilim/Second Temple; Scripture connections + Hebrew lemmas; scholarship verification + synthesis). Status in-review; no merge, publish, or deploy by the drafter. Claim count: 49 — arithmetic: dossier §9 register has 113 rows (clm-hc-001…113); 48 taken verbatim plus 1 adapted (016, trimmed of the cross-dossier flag) = 49. Excluded: 8 assessed not-independently-verified (003, 007, 013, 020, 028, 030, 036, 043) — excluded from the article by rule; 10 dossier-only rows (038, 062, 063, 069, 075, 076, 077, 082, 095, 106); 46 verified-but-not-used rows (009, 019, 022, 023, 026, 027, 031, 032, 033, 034, 035, 037, 039, 041, 044, 045, 046, 047, 048, 052, 054, 056, 057, 058, 060, 061, 064, 065, 066, 067, 068, 071, 072, 085, 086, 087, 093, 094, 097, 103, 107, 108, 110, 111, 112, 113) — of which 031, 032, 033, 034, 035, 037, 039 are the Second Temple reception claims, held dossier-only per the conservative decision below. Word counts are the validator's countWords method, which includes the four Ancient World subsection headings. The .md prose was trimmed to the validator's 200–400 word range for Ancient World (the first draft counted 781); the full holder lists, the Enlil and Namzitarra 120-year parallel, and the 'also after that' discussion are carried in the register (clm-hc-040/042, clm-hc-096) and the dossier, not in the prose. Quotation accounting: the .md prose contains no Scripture quotation (paraphrase only, per published precedent); the passage's own terms (Nephilim, mighty men) are used unquoted as terms, not as quotations. Connection-note quotations are short KJV phrases from ranges verified in the stored KJV. The one non-Scripture quotation in the register, 'the gods gathered like flies' (Thompson 1928, Gilgamesh XI), is confirmed verbatim and recorded in clm-hc-016's evidence. 1 Enoch's 'three thousand ells' is NOT quoted anywhere (dossier-only). Second-hand labelling: Neofiti renderings are second-hand via Newman 1984 citing Diez Macho (clm-hc-081 evidence); the Ugaritic assembly phrases beyond KTU 1.4, the rpum identification, the Uruk List pairings, the Egyptian 110-year ideal, the Atrahasis 'noise' motive, Gilgamesh's 'eleven cubits', Humbaba, and Jubilees 4:15/7:21–22 are not-independently-verified and do not enter the article; Westermann on Gen 6:4 (partial, two find-result lines) and on Gen 6:5–8 (not reached) are dossier-only (clm-hc-095/106); the 1 Enoch/Jubilees dating (c. 3rd/2nd century BCE) is probable (consensus), no dating monograph consulted. Conservative decisions applied (flagged for Yonatan, not assumed): (1) all three 'sons of God' readings presented with no endorsement; (2) 1 Enoch/Jubilees/Book of Giants material stays dossier-only — the public article names neither 1 Enoch nor Jubilees (clm-hc-079's register evidence records the full Westermann/Gunkel position including the 1 Enoch channel; clm-hc-101's register evidence records Jubilees 5:8 as a text-critical witness; the prose names neither); (3) 'Nephilim' is the article's term, 'giants' noted as the KJV rendering; (4) relatedEvents one-way to existing events only (Seth, Adam and Eve, Creation) — the Gen 6:9–22 sequel is a Scripture connection (conn-hc-003), not a relatedEvents link, and no link is added to the not-yet-existing Flood event; (5) narrativeOrder 6 as proposed. Disagreements preserved as debated, not resolved: the three readings (DQ-01), the Nephilim etymology and identity (DQ-02/03), the 120 years (DQ-04), yādôn (DQ-05), divine repentance in emphasis (DQ-06), the passage's relation to the Flood (DQ-07), 'also after that' (DQ-12), Noah's favour (DQ-13). Dossier-only material: the endpoint/BDB discrepancies (062, 063), the H582 row (075), H2580 BDB not consulted (069), HALOT/DCH not consulted (077) — no exception has been granted for this event (the A&E exception does not extend); the royal reading's modern-scholarship holder gap (082); the six modern commentaries (Wenham, Hamilton, Sarna, Cassuto, von Rad, Brueggemann) plus Waltke, Mathews, Sailhamer, Kugel, Collins, VanderKam, Nickelsburg (2001) — none accessible in full text, no position attributed; Chrysostom Homily 22, Augustine De Genesi ad litteram, Cyril Glaphyra 2.1 — inaccessible, no position attributed; no Crouch 2016 reuse. Connections: 11/11 verified against the stored KJV (dossier §11); rejected 6 stay rejected (Gen 3:15, Gen 1:26–28, Deut 32:8 as a connection, 1 Pet 3:19–20 handed to the Flood event, Luke 17:26–27 as a near-duplicate of Matt 24:37–39, Gen 11:1–9); all reception connections (008, 009, 010) label the link as reception, never as what Genesis 6 itself says; conn-hc-003 is a one-way link to the Gen 6:9–22 event (Dev 2's record, not edited); conn-hc-006 carries the spies'-report cautions and does not assert the Anakim as distinct from the Nephilim. Sources: 19 cited (8 existing: BDB, Westermann, Keil & Delitzsch, Ryle, Skinner, Gunkel, JFB, Clarke — reused as-is, no entry edited; their Gen 6:1–8 consultation is recorded in the claim evidence and here, and the EM may consider verificationDetail appends per the #194 precedent; 11 new: Hendel, Thompson Gilgamesh, ETCSL Death of Gilgamesh, ETCSL Šulgi, ETCSL Eridu Genesis, Baal Cycle, Berossus, Sibbing-Plantholt, Augustine City of God, Targum Onkelos, Rashi). Fathers and Jewish sources other than Augustine, Onkelos, and Rashi are named in claim evidence with dossier §12.1 references, following the Seth precedent for evidence naming works outside the registry (Justin, Tertullian, Irenaeus, Athenagoras, Africanus, Eusebius, Philo, Josephus, Genesis Rabbah, Ibn Ezra, Jewish Encyclopedia, Newman 1984 as intermediary for Neofiti). The Atrahasis contrast (clm-hc-019) is not cited here — no registry entry exists for it; the flood contrast rests on Gilgamesh XI, Eridu Genesis, and Berossus. The Gilgamesh XI cross-dossier flag (Cain and Abel dossier §3.5c 'NOT-INDEPENDENTLY-VERIFIED' now stale — Tablet XI verified in full here) is the EM's to action. No editorialOverride is granted or presumed (in-review status).
